THE ORDINARY-WORK MATRIX AND THE ADVANCED CENSUS DISAGREE, AND THE CENSUS IS THE PRODUCT. The 54-case matrix is 17 REAL / 0 FALSE / 0 DAMAGED at a 172 ms median; a new 49-request census of advanced software work -- C/C++/Rust/Go/Java, build, CI, performance, concurrency, test authoring, git surgery, design -- serves 2, one of them wrongly. Five rows absorb 24 of the 49 selections and then refuse their own inputs, and whole domains have zero rows of 440. The census is now an instrument in the tree so the number is repeatable, and the two matrix cases whose own sentences authorise the files they change no longer report damage.

THE GATE REFUSED AN ANSWER THE MACHINE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN. The symbol index emits a 105.8 MB artifact for canonical/runtime in which the callers answer is 1.47 MB, and the answer gate's 16 MB cap refused the whole run -- 16.5-18.7 s to ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE while the same sentence about one file answered in 293 ms. The index's own cache, meanwhile, was keyed by the request's artifact path, which the door makes unique per request, so no two sentences about one tree ever shared work. Neither fix is a new primitive: the gate already projects and bounds an answer, and the index already had a sha256-verified row cache looking for a key a caller could repeat.

intents.summary: 'Write the content X to the output path <f>' was answered by docx.document.verify.intent_ooxml, which raised DOCX_INTENT_SIDECAR_MISSING. Its keywords include 'content', 'exact', 'word' and 'document', so the sentence matched -- and its only declared input is a path, so it could be bound ONLY once that path existed. The identical sentence over a path that did not yet exist was served correctly by the text writer. A file's mere existence changed which capability answered an ordinary write. Keep the record of a step whose adapter raised, and report it as work whose outcome is unknown instead of as a goal that could not be made executable, so no report ever denies a side effect that landed.

composer_route_v1.execute_chain read a step's output as result.get('result'), but run_adapter_locally returns the adapter's own dict AS the result -- output_path, output_sha256, output_verified, output_bytes -- and never wraps it under a 'result' key. So observed was None for every step of every chain. Two measured consequences: the step record was written as {'raw': null}, destroying the only evidence the step produced, and `produced` stayed empty, so bind could never offer a later step anything an earlier step had made -- the mechanism multi-step composition exists for. The chain still returned pass=True, so a composed goal answered 'done' while its own record said nothing had been produced, and nothing downstream could verify it because there was nothing to verify. The step now records the adapter's real result, minus the two keys run_adapter_locally stamps itself (capability_id, dependency), which describe the invocation and must not become bindable slots.

failure_reason answers why a goal failed but not whose fault it is, and those are different questions. A refusal means the system behaved correctly; an adapter fault means the system has a bug. Both were reported as LIVE_CONTROLLER_EXECUTION_OR_VERIFICATION_FAILURE, so a caller and the learning loop could not tell them apart. failure_kind now classifies every failure as ADAPTER_FAULT, ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKER, CONTRACT_REFUSAL or UNKNOWN. The caught fault set is the programming-error family and nothing else: RuntimeError and ValueError are the adapters' own contract vocabulary (355 and 72 deliberate raise sites) and Blocker subclasses RuntimeError, so either would destroy 427 named errors. A named error is recognised by its SHAPE -- an identifier followed by a colon, or an UPPER_SNAKE token -- because enumerating names cannot work and a marker list measured 17 of 60 failures as UNKNOWN that were perfectly well named.

intents.summary: Learned-once is now fast on the NEXT machine. The transfer store was gated on an equality test: `similarity` returned 0.0 unless two environments had byte-identical action sets and state shapes, so the same computer with ONE extra binary on PATH -- which changes the 14 programs a fingerprint acts out -- could not recall anything it had learned, and a different goal's shortlist (16 actions) could not match another goal's (40 actions) on the SAME machine. Measured before: similarity 0.0, recall []. Measured after: similarity 0.93, recall returns the plan, and a goal learned cold in 7,147 ms is answered in 699 ms on an image with a different program inventory. Two smaller defects fixed with it: a recalled plan naming a program this machine does not have is no longer replayed (it would have been recorded as DISPROVEN, poisoning the row that would work once the program was installed), and the fingerprint's shortlist is now read as a SAMPLE of the machine rather than the whole of it.

THE GATE REFUSED AN ANSWER THE MACHINE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN. The symbol index emits a 105.8 MB artifact for canonical/runtime in which the callers answer is 1.47 MB, and the answer gate's 16 MB cap refused the whole run -- 16.5-18.7 s to ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE while the same sentence about one file answered in 293 ms. The index's own cache, meanwhile, was keyed by the request's artifact path, which the door makes unique per request, so no two sentences about one tree ever shared work. Neither fix is a new primitive: the gate already projects and bounds an answer, and the index already had a sha256-verified row cache looking for a key a caller could repeat.

A sentence that names no capability -- 'Write the text hello to the file notes.txt' -- matches no single capability, so the composer answers it with a chain. That path reported pass=True on the strength of the chain having run, with no acceptance verdict of any kind. The front-layer local adapter path was fixed in #6111 and the model-independent controller path in #6112; this was the third and last path that never asked, and it is the one ordinary requests actually take. It could not ask before for two concrete reasons, both now gone: the step records were {'raw': null} so there was no evidence to inspect (#6115), and no acceptance contract was ever built here -- compile_contract derives one from the sentence alone but refuses with ROUTING_TARGET_EFFECTS_EMPTY unless told which files the request touches, measured as 0 obligations with an empty effect set and 2 with the step's own output_path. And text.file.write, the capability those sentences reach, had no re-inspector. This adds one -- it re-derives the expected bytes from the REQUEST's own content argument and compares them to the file on disk, never consulting output_verified or output_sha256, which only prove the file is what the writer wrote rather than what was asked for -- and wires the composed path to build the contract from the effects the chain actually declared, put the trace in the canonical row shape with a finish row, and report what the verifier says.

PR #6111 fixed the front-layer local adapter path, which hard-coded semantic_acceptance_complete False and never called the acceptance verifier. Its sibling in the same module, the model-independent controller path, carried the identical line and the identical omission. Measured on bf2799b over the 51 capabilities that declare an output artifact with every input stated: 9 pass, all 9 write the promised file, 3 reach exact semantic acceptance, and 5 carry no acceptance verdict at all -- two of them (auto.npm.dfinity-cbor, auto.npm.msgpack-msgpack) take the controller path, pass, write their artifact and were never asked. The controller path now asks the verifier. Its trace already carries the canonical shape, so unlike the front-layer path nothing about the trace needed repairing, only asking.

Every phrasing that happened to work did so by luck, because 'text', 'content' and 'output' are keywords of the text writer. The tiebreak now demotes a JSON token when the sentence states a payload the brain already reads as text, after the score and never before it. The whole write family -- six role words crossed with ten destination phrasings -- went to 60 of 60.

Ambient (implicit) agent context via ``contextvars``. Threading an explicit ``ctx`` handle through an agent is the most transparent API, but many frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, …) own the call stack and give you no place to pass one. The ambient context solves that: the recorder and replayer publish the active :class:`~agent_replay.recorder.AgentContext` here for the duration of a run, and instrumented callables (see :mod:`agent_replay.instrument`) pick it up implicitly. It is a plain ``contextvars.ContextVar`` so it is correct across threads and ``asyncio`` tasks.

The ablation engine: stochastic run-forward under a replay plan. Because the agent policy is stochastic, a single intervention does not yield one outcome but an *outcome distribution*. The engine executes a plan ``rollouts`` times with independent seeds and returns the per-rollout failure indicators, from which the scorer estimates ``P(fail | ...)`` together with its uncertainty.

The attribution scorer: turn ablation rollouts into a causal verdict. Two estimators are implemented, matching the paper: **Phase 1 — single-step contrastive estimation.** For every candidate step ``i`` we hold ``< i`` factual, resample ``>= i``, and compute attribution(i) = P(fail | kept) - P(fail | ablated from i) with a Wilson interval on the ablated failure rate and a bootstrap interval on the difference. The *magnitude* of this score is deliberately **not** used to pick the culprit: resampling an early step re-rolls the fatal late step too (the butterfly-effect confound), inflating early
Exception types for agent-replay.

Canonical content hashing and Merkle-style linking. Every recorded value is reduced to a deterministic SHA-256 over its canonical JSON form. Equal values therefore share an address, which is what lets the checkpoint store deduplicate blobs (content-addressable storage) and lets each step chain off its parent, giving the trajectory a tamper-evident identity.

Recording: capture an agent run as a replayable trajectory. The public contract is a small ``AgentContext`` handed to the user's agent function. The agent performs its work through ``ctx.llm(...)``, ``ctx.tool(...)`` and ``ctx.memory(...)``, passing a ``produce`` callable that *is* the stochastic policy for that step. During recording the policy is executed and its output is stored; during replay the very same agent code runs, but the context decides — per step — whether to serve the recorded output (deterministic replay) or to re-run the policy (a counterfactual resample). Crucially, the agen

Deterministic replay with counterfactual interventions. A :class:`ReplayPlan` decides, for every recorded step, whether the recorded action is *held* at its factual value (served from the cassette) or *ablated*. The core attribution move — "hold all prior steps at their factual recorded actions, apply the intervention, and execute the trajectory forward" — is a plan that holds ``{0..i-1}`` and resamples everything from ``i`` onward. Statistical estimators used by the attribution scorer. The paper insists on reporting *bounded* marginal contributions: a Wilson score interval for the success proportion of the stochastic rollouts, and a bootstrap interval on the difference between the factual and counterfactual failure distributions. Both are implemented here with the standard library only.

Core data types for agent-replay. An agent execution is formalised (following the *Trajectory Causal Attribution* paper) as a Structural Causal Model: a sequence of steps, each of which reads a context, draws an action from a stochastic policy, and observes a result. These dataclasses are the serialisable backbone that the recorder, store, replayer, ablation engine and attribution scorer all share.

Bounded model-free finance metric -> SEC XBRL concept registry. The registry maps only explicit finance metric aliases to finite standard taxonomy candidate sets. It does not infer issuer-specific extension meaning, choose among multiple surviving concepts, or claim a source fact is correct. A downstream source-native SEC capability must fetch candidate concepts and a separate selector must prove a unique period-bound fact before arithmetic use.

Formula-implied dependency compiler for donor-free finance workflows. Takes the explicit operation/metric contract and adds only dependencies forced by the formula definition. It distinguishes standard SEC facts, market prices, question literals, and semantic/custom-source obligations.

Compile explicit finance-question structure into model-free typed contracts. This compiler recognizes only operations literally requested or unambiguously named in the question. It does not infer hidden benchmark categories, source facts, industry conventions, or qualitative conclusions. AA-Briefcase current-evidence parity indistinguishability certificate. The certifier proves a narrow epistemic result. Therefore a just-below-target result and a target-meeting result remain observationally indistinguishable from the current retained evidence. A future verified score or genuinely new scope-complete premise reopens this cut.

Fail-closed weakest-sufficient residual theorem compiler. Given independently verified finite Horn implications and already-proved baseline facts, derive exact minimal primitive residual fact sets sufficient to prove each target. Unlike minimum_terminal_basis_v1, residual facts need not be predeclared as candidate facts. They are synthesized from the leaves of the verified implication graph. This module never invents semantic edges, scope relations, metric bindings, or credit.

Exact acceptance backpropagation for frozen binary benchmark populations. This compiler reverses a frozen binary-rate acceptance threshold into the weakest remaining success mass required after independently verified proof/observation partitions are applied. Positive partitions must bind explicit frozen population slot IDs to an independently verified scope-complete content-addressed receipt. The compiler recomputes the frozen population commitment, requires every partition to bind that exact commitment, and rejects overlap so a slot can never be counted twice. The output is scheduling evidenc

Fail-closed conservative acceptance bound compiler. Purpose: - determine whether a frozen fixed-bar acceptance result can be forced from a strict subset of executable observations; - assign worst-case values to unavailable/unexecuted slots; - expose exact pass/fail locks without extrapolation. This module never grants capability/family credit by itself.

Fail-closed capability-source gate for Opus 5.5 acceptance benchmark execution. A public/free benchmark harness is not enough. The candidate being measured must also be a Brain-owned, donor-independent capability route. This gate prevents spending clean benchmark cases on adapters whose operative cognition is external.

Fail-closed source gate for Opus 5.5 acceptance execution. Canonical ownership forbids another model from supplying producer cognition for any Brain-credited acceptance result. Model locality, openness, hosting, wrapping, or content addressing does not change attribution.

Delimit routing prose from an explicit measured-acceptance contract. The live capability registry binds ``task_text`` to ``${input.goal}``. A goal that both names its filesystem bindings and states its acceptance predicates is therefore one string with two grammars: Write a report to R for source root S using test path T where `tests_pass` must be true and `python_parse_ok` must be true The lossless acceptance layer is correct to treat the binding prefix as unresolved semantics. Deleting that prefix inside the acceptance layer would also silently delete a hidden requirement, so this module doe

Compile atomic Opus55 gaps into a fail-closed executable action frontier. This layer never grants capability/family credit. It recomputes the live atomic residual from canonical inputs, emits one exact gap certificate per predicate, and ranks only explicitly declared actions. It does not invent semantic proof implications or guess wall-clock durations.

Canonical zero-credit acceptance IR compiler. Compiles the frozen atomic predicate registry, content-addressed evidence bindings, and the active action hypergraph into one deterministic scheduling IR. This module does not infer semantic equivalence, create acceptance evidence, authorize benchmark execution, or grant capability/family credit.

Compile a proof-first terminal action frontier. This layer does not perform semantic theorem proving. It enforces ordering: bounded zero-reality proof compilation/search actions that can affect unresolved predicates outrank fresh acceptance-case execution. Reality is queried only after the declared proof-first actions have either closed their target or are explicitly saturated/exhausted.

Fail-closed stronger-proof replacement planner for frozen acceptance predicates. This planner does not invent benchmark equivalence, scope coverage, probabilities, or acceptance credit. It composes existing independently-verified proof compilers to find whether a candidate stronger witness already implies a frozen target, and otherwise returns the smallest zero-reality attempt frontier in a fixed proof-precedence order. It is planning-only. A passing candidate remains zero-credit until separately bound by the canonical acceptance authority.

Fail-closed proof transmutation compiler for Project Brain Opus 5.5 acceptance. Scheduling/proof-routing authority only. Never grants capability or family credit. A stronger proof may satisfy an unchanged frozen protocol only when the witness is verified, independent, contamination-clean, binds the frozen protocol, and covers the entire protocol scope. Behavioral-only evidence can never close ownership.

Fail-closed verifier for acceptance-complete quotient simulation. This verifies only a finite abstract certificate. It does not prove that the abstraction is sound or that abstract Brain macrosteps are universally realizable; those facts must be supplied by independent, scope-complete receipts and are treated as load-bearing premises.

Semantic hardening wrapper for acceptance-quotient simulation V1. V1 checks finite graph simulation but does not, by itself, certify that the declared relation is a material noninferiority relation or that scope/authority holds for each realizing macroedge. V2 makes those semantic premises explicit content-addressed receipt obligations before delegating graph mechanics to V1. This remains a structural verifier: independent receipt files must themselves be verified on their exact bytes before any acceptance credit.

Causal-strategy hardening wrapper for acceptance-quotient simulation V2. V2 binds graph simulation to semantic noninferiority/scope receipts, but the underlying graph mechanics are still pointwise existential: for each target edge, some matching Brain macroedge may be selected. That is insufficient for an owned agent unless all such matches are induced by one causal Brain policy whose choices depend only on information available at the decision prefix. V3 makes that uniform-strategy premise explicit and fail-closed. It remains a structural verifier: the referenced policy-binding receipt bytes

Acceptance-class gate over causal-strategy quotient simulation V3. V3 prevents per-target-edge oracle selection by requiring one owned causal policy. V4 additionally binds the acceptance semantics class so stochastic matched noninferiority cannot be inferred from structural/causal trace simulation unless a policy-level distribution, stochastic-dominance, or expected-utility bridge is independently certified. This module verifies receipt shape only. Exact receipt bytes remain a separate independent promotion gate.

Policy-identity hardening for acceptance-quotient simulation V4. V3 requires a single causal policy semantically, but neither V3 nor V4 mechanically ties the global strategy receipt, per-edge policy bindings, and policy-distribution receipt to the same policy identity. V5 closes that referential-integrity gap with a content commitment. This remains a structural verifier. Referenced receipt bytes require separate independent verification before any acceptance credit.

Generic forbidden-action guard and execution-trace verifier. This module is benchmark-agnostic. Independent generic goal-state verifier for Project Brain. This verifier checks post-action observations against the compiled goal contract. Identity-bound generic post-state verifier for Project Brain. V2 verifies both positive goals and negative constraints. It is independent from planning, argument binding, and execution. Where a constraint cannot be independently established from post-state evidence, verification fails closed rather than assuming compliance.

Generic goal-state verifier V3 with complete execution-trace constraints. Is this claim about the machine actually true? Re-read it and find out. Every other capability here is verified against something the machine attests. A claim about a system was not. It could be asserted, and nothing checked it, which is the one place where the system could agree with itself. "Not Self-Decidable" (arXiv:2610.04699) puts it exactly: a check over a field the agent asserts establishes only that the agent agreed with itself. Anytime-valid Bernoulli confidence sequence for H100 proposal viability. Uses exact Clopper-Pearson bounds with summable alpha spending. For two-sided confidence level 1-alpha, each side receives alpha/2 and time t receives alpha_side/(t*(t+1)). Since sum_{t>=1} 1/(t(t+1)) = 1, a union bound gives simultaneous coverage over every stopping time without optional-stopping leakage. This is intentionally conservative and dependency-free. It is an operational stopping instrument, not open-world evidence and not capability credit.

Capability-ratcheted search bounds for H100. A verified deterministic capability library can shorten future proposal descriptions without adding persistent learned bytes. This is a formal storage/compute tradeoff result, not a claim that every real task belongs to a compiled family.

Information-theoretic lexical no-evidence bound for H100. If a novel term has no distinguishing evidence, two semantic worlds may expose the exact same observation while assigning different canonical roles to that term. Any decision rule receiving that identical observation must therefore behave identically in both worlds. A forced role is wrong in at least one world; abstention is the only fail-closed answer valid across both. This is an information bound, not a model-size claim.
